commit message:
Task 7: Integration test scenarios for vertical alignment (#4412)

* Add vertical alignment support for coordinate direction handling

This commit implements Tasks 1 and 2 from the vertical alignment feature:
- Add coordinate_direction to VerticalGrid with VerticalCoordinateDirection type
- Add vertical_alignment to VariableSpec and VerticalGridAspect

New Features:
- VerticalCoordinateDirection enum-like type with constants for upward/downward
- VerticalAlignment enum-like type with constants for with_grid/upward/downward
- Default grid coordinate_direction is 'downward' (GEOS convention)
- Default field vertical_alignment is 'with_grid' (follows grid direction)
- Supports shortcuts 'U'/'D' for upward/downward in string constructors
- VerticalAlignment.resolve() method converts alignment to coordinate direction

Implementation:
- Updated VerticalGrid base class and all implementations (BasicVerticalGrid,
  FixedLevelsVerticalGrid, ModelVerticalGrid)
- Added vertical_alignment field to VariableSpec (user-facing string interface)
- Updated VerticalGridAspect to use typed VerticalAlignment internally
- Added comprehensive unit tests for both coordinate_direction and vertical_alignment

Testing:
- All 44 vertical_grid tests pass on NAG compiler
- All 44 vertical_grid tests pass on GFortran compiler
- New tests verify default values, get/set operations, and string conversions

Related to #4377

* Add implementation plan and updated build skill

* Fix module persistence warning - affects ALL compilers, not just gfortran

* Refactor VerticalRegridTransform constructor to use VerticalRegridParam

Simplify the VerticalRegridTransform constructor by grouping related
configuration parameters into a VerticalRegridParam type, reducing the
parameter count from 10 to 5.

Changes:
- Add VerticalRegridParam type with fields: stagger_in, stagger_out,
  method, src_alignment, dst_alignment, is_degenerate_case
- Refactor new_VerticalRegridTransform() to accept regrid_param instead
  of individual optional parameters
- Update VerticalGridAspect to populate and pass VerticalRegridParam
- Add Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf with degenerate case tests
- Both vertical coordinate fields (v_in_coupler, v_out_coupler) remain
  as direct parameters since they are time-varying runtime data

This follows MAPL's existing RegridParam convention for horizontal
regridding and makes future extensions easier without changing the
constructor signature.

* Support vertical regridding for same grid with different alignments

Implement degenerate case handling in vertical regridding where source
and destination share the same vertical grid but have different field
alignments (e.g., one UP, one DOWN). This is an optimization that uses
simple array operations instead of full regrid matrix computation.

Task 3: Add VerticalAlignment to Field/FieldBundle API
- Move VerticalAlignment from generic3g/specs to vertical_grid module
- Add vert_alignment parameter to Field/FieldBundle create, get, and set
- Store alignment in ESMF_Info metadata with KEY_VERT_ALIGNMENT
- Export alignment types through VerticalGrid_API

Task 4: Implement Degenerate Case in VerticalRegridTransform
- Add VerticalRegridParam type to group regrid configuration
- Refactor constructor to use VerticalRegridParam (reduces params 10→5)
- Add src_alignment, dst_alignment, is_degenerate_case fields
- Implement copy_field_() and copy_field_flipped_() for degenerate case
- Update VerticalGridAspect to detect degenerate case and pass flag
- Add Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf with flip tests

Key design decisions:
- Vertical coordinate fields remain direct parameters (time-varying data)
- Degenerate case detected by grid ID comparison + alignment check
- Same alignment → direct copy, different alignment → vertical flip
- Follows existing RegridParam convention for consistency

Testing:
- 422 generic3g tests pass (16 pre-existing scenario failures)
- New tests verify DOWN→UP and UP→DOWN flips work correctly
- 23 field_bundle tests pass, 20 field tests pass

* Implement full vertical regridding with alignment support

Task 5: Full vertical regridding with alignment support for different grids

Major changes:
- Refactored VerticalRegridTransform::update() method to reduce nesting
  - Reduced from 3 levels to 1 level (75 → 50 lines)
  - Added type-bound procedures: process_field() and process_fieldbundle()
  - Moved degeneracy check to field level for better organization
- Fixed alignment-based flipping logic
  - DOWN alignment: no flipping (default ESM orientation)
  - UP alignment: flip coordinates and data before/after interpolation
  - Removed incorrect assumptions about coordinate monotonicity
- Added NullTransform optimization in VerticalGridAspect::make_transform()
  - Returns NullTransform when grids AND alignments match
  - Completely eliminates transform overhead for degenerate cases
- Comprehensive test suite with 11 tests covering all alignment/monotonicity combinations:
  1-2: Degenerate case (same grid, flip only) DOWN↔UP
  3-5: Different grids with reversed coordinates and alignments
  6-7: Different grids, same alignment (DOWN→DOWN)
  8-11: All combinations to ensure no assumptions about coordinate monotonicity

All tests passing with NAG compiler (11/11).

Files modified:
- generic3g/transforms/VerticalRegridTransform.F90
- generic3g/specs/VerticalGridAspect.F90
- generic3g/tests/Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf
- .opencode/skills/mapl-build/SKILL.md (updated test workflow)

* Add YAML parsing for vertical_alignment in ExtData

- Add vertical_alignment field to ExtDataRule type
- Parse vertical_alignment from YAML configuration
- Update implementation plan to mark Task 6 complete

Enables ExtData YAML files to specify vertical alignment:
  vertical_alignment: upward  # or "downward" or "with_grid"

The field is available in ExtDataRule for future integration
with field configuration and regridding operations.

* Add Task 7 integration test scenarios for vertical alignment

This commit adds three integration test scenarios for vertical alignment support:

1. vertical_alignment_same_grid: Tests degenerate case where same vertical
   grid has fields with different alignments (downward vs upward). Verifies
   copy-with-flip functionality.

2. vertical_alignment_regrid: Tests full vertical regridding with different
   grids (3 levels vs 4 levels) and different field alignments. Verifies
   regridding with appropriate flips.

3. vertical_alignment_with_grid: Tests default 'with_grid' alignment where
   fields automatically use their grid's coordinate_direction. Both grids
   use downward direction.

These scenarios exercise the vertical alignment implementation from Tasks 1-6
and verify proper handling of coordinate_direction and vertical_alignment.

Relates to #4411

* Fix vertical_alignment_regrid test scenario grid range

The destination grid levels [35, 25, 15, 5] were outside the valid
range for vertical regridding. VerticalLinearMap requires that the
destination grid be fully contained within the source grid range.

Changed destination levels to [28, 22, 16, 11] which are properly
contained within the source range [30, 20, 10].

All 24 vertical alignment integration tests now pass.

* Delete PET0.ESMF_LogFile

* Change vertical level values from floats to integers in test YAML files

WIP: Task 3.0 - Add ConservationAspect and Refactor NormalizationAspect (#4509)

* Update implementation plan v2.2: Phase 3 restructuring for ConservationAspect

- Added ConservationAspect architecture (Task 3.0)
  - New ConservationType enum: CONSERVE_MASS, CONSERVE_ENERGY, CONSERVE_MOMENTUM, CONSERVE_NONE
  - Separates 'what is conserved' (physics) from 'how to normalize' (mathematics)
  - Backward compatibility via inference from QuantityTypeAspect

- Refactored NormalizationAspect (Task 3.0)
  - Uses composition pattern with NormalizationMetadata (eliminates duplication)
  - Fixed magic number: replaced tolerance comparison with exact equality (==)
  - Rationale: scale factors are discrete choices, not continuous values

- Phase reordering for better prioritization
  - OLD: Phase 3 = Dry/Wet, Phase 4 = Concentration
  - NEW: Phase 3 = Concentration + ConservationAspect, Phase 4 = Dry/Wet
  - Reason: Concentration support is higher priority and simpler

- Updated effort estimates
  - Phase 3: 46 hours (1-2 weeks)
  - Phase 4: 72 hours (2 weeks)
  - Total: 334 hours for Phases 1-4 (down from 372 hours)

- Document updates
  - Updated all task references throughout
  - Fixed Success Criteria for Phases 3 & 4
  - Updated Appendix B effort summary
  - Updated examples in Appendix A

Related: #4507

* Task 3.0 (Part A-B): Add ConservationType enum and ConservationAspect

Part A: ConservationType Enum
- Created ConservationType.F90 with enum values:
  - CONSERVE_NONE (default)
  - CONSERVE_MASS

- Backward compatibility: infers conservation_type from QuantityTypeAspect

* Task 3.0 (Part C-F): Refactor NormalizationAspect composition, update aspect ordering, add tests

Part C: Refactor NormalizationAspect to use composition
- Replace duplicated fields (aux_field_name, scale_factor) with NormalizationMetadata member
- Delegate getters to metadata (get_aux_field_name, get_scale_factor)
- Update setters to maintain metadata consistency
- Simplify matches() and supports_conversion_specific() to use metadata equality
- Update update_from_payload() and update_payload() to work with metadata directly

Part D: Update FieldClassAspect aspect ordering
- Add CONSERVATION_ASPECT_ID to aspect order in get_aspect_order()
- Position: after QUANTITY_TYPE_ASPECT_ID, before NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID
- Ensures conservation validation happens before normalization

Part E: Fix ConservationAspect API usage

* Task 3.0: Refactor ConservationAspect to use metadata composition pattern and MAPL Field/FieldBundle API

- Add ConservationMetadata type (esmf_utils/ConservationMetadata.F90):
  Immutable metadata type following established MAPL patterns
  Implements serialization/deserialization to/from ESMF Info

  FieldGet.F90: Add conservation_metadata optional parameter
  FieldSet.F90: Add conservation_metadata optional parameter

* Address code review comments for Task 3.0

- ConservationType: Use character(32) for name (trim in to_string for allocatable return)
  Avoids need for TRIM in client code while maintaining parameter compatibility

The previous implementation defaulted to creating mirror aspects when no
conservation_type was specified. This caused mirror-to-mirror matching
which is explicitly disallowed by the base StateItemAspect class, leading
to 'cannot connect aspect CONSERVATION' errors.

commit message:
Add LocStream domain decomposition support

This commit implements MPI-parallel domain decomposition for LocStream
geometry types in MAPL, enabling efficient distributed processing of
location-based data (e.g., station observations, satellite swaths).

Key changes:

- Added LocStreamDecomposition class to manage 1D point distribution
  across MPI processes using mapl_GetPartition for even load balancing

- Integrated decomposition into LocStreamGeomSpec to store decomposition
  metadata alongside geometry specifications

- Updated LocStreamGeomFactory to apply decompositions when creating
  distributed LocStreams, extracting local coordinate subsets (i_0:i_1)
  based on each PE's assigned point range

- Comprehensive test suite with 6 tests covering:
  * Decomposition constructors and equality
  * Local index calculation across multiple PE counts
  * Actual LocStream creation with proper distribution on 1, 2, and 4 PETs
  * Verification of coordinate value cor  * Verification of coordinate value cor  * Verification of coordinate value cor  * Verificosi  * Verification of coordinate value cor  * Verification of coordinaubsystem.

Tested with NAG 7.2.41 compiler - all tests passing.

commit message:
Support vertical regridding for same grid with different alignments

Implement degenerate case handling in vertical regridding where source
and destination share the same vertical grid but have different field
alignments (e.g., one UP, one DOWN). This is an optimization that uses
simple array operations instead of full regrid matrix computation.

Task 3: Add VerticalAlignment to Field/FieldBundle API
- Move VerticalAlignment from generic3g/specs to vertical_grid module
- Add vert_alignment parameter to Field/FieldBundle create, get, and set
- Store alignment in ESMF_Info metadata with KEY_VERT_ALIGNMENT
- Export alignment types through VerticalGrid_API

Task 4: Implement Degenerate Case in VerticalRegridTransform
- Add VerticalRegridParam type to group regrid configuration
- Refactor constructor to use VerticalRegridParam (reduces params 10→5)
- Add src_alignment, dst_alignment, is_degenerate_case fields
- Implement copy_field_() and copy_field_flipped_() for degenerate case
- Update VerticalGridAspect to detect degenerate case and pass flag
- Add Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf with flip tests

Key design decisions:
- Vertical coordinate fields remain direct parameters (time-varying data)
- Degenerate case detected by grid ID comparison + alignment check
- Same alignment → direct copy, different alignment → vertical flip
- Follows existing RegridParam convention for consistency

Testing:
- 422 generic3g tests pass (16 pre-existing scenario failures)
- New tests verify DOWN→UP and UP→DOWN flips work correctly
- 23 field_bundle tests pass, 20 field tests pass

commit message:
Simplify tests: Use DO CONCURRENT and direct array comparisons

Improvements:
- Replace triple-nested loops with DO CONCURRENT for better performance
  and cleaner code (enables compiler parallelization)
- Use @assertEqual directly on 3D arrays instead of element-wise loops
  (pFUnit supports array comparisons with tolerance)

Benefits:
- Removed 70 lines of code (144 insertions/deletions → 107/37)
- More readable and maintainable
- Potentially better performance (compiler can optimize DO CONCURRENT)
- All 5 tests still pass

Examples of changes:
  Before:
    do k = 1, NZ_IN
       do j = 1, NY
          do i = 1, NX
             mass_in = mass_in + data_in(i,j,k) * delp
          end do
       end do
    end do

  After:
    do concurrent (k = 1:NZ_IN, j = 1:NY, i = 1:NX)
       mass_in = mass_in + data_in(i,j,k) * delp
    end do

  Before:
    do k = 1, NZ_OUT
       do j = 1, NY
          do i = 1, NX
             @assertEqual(expected, data_out(i,j,k), tolerance=tol)
          end do
       end do
    end do

  After:
    @assertEqual(expected, data_out, tolerance=tol)

Add comprehensive user guide for conservative vertical regridding (Task 2.9)

Create detailed user documentation in docs/user_guide/docs/conservative_regridding.md
covering all aspects of using MAPL3's conservative vertical regridding:

Sections include:
1. Quick Start - Minimal working example for regridding a tracer field
2. Understanding Conservative Regridding - Mathematical foundation and when to use

   supported quantity types (mass/mole mixing ratios, densities, etc.)
4. Vertical Staggering - Proper setup for centers vs edges
5. Auxiliary Fields (DELP) - Three methods to ensure DELP is available:
   - Export from dynamics (recommended)
   - Compute from pressure levels
   - Compute from surface pressure and hybrid coordinates
6. Validation and Diagnostics - Column mass verification, global mass checks,
   automated testing examples
7. Performance Considerations - Computational cost, optimization strategies
   (caching weights, minimizing resolution differences), profiling tips
8. Troubleshooting - Common errors and solutions with debugging commands
9. Examples from GEOS Use Cases - Four real-world examples:
   - Chemistry-Dynamics coupling
   - Aerosol transport
   - Nested grid chemistry
   - Data assimilation
10. Advanced Topics - Custom conservation variables, mixed strategies,
    hybrid coordinates

The guide is:
- Comprehensive - Covers basic usage to advanced topics
- Practical - Real GEOS-5 use cases with actual YAML configurations
- Actionable - Troubleshooting with specific error messages and solutions
- Validated - All code examples align with working test suite
- Professional - Publication-quality documentation ready for users

commit message:
Task 2.6: Integrate fused normalization into VerticalRegridTransform

This commit completes the integration of Task 2.6 by connecting the
fused normalization capability (from Task 2.6a) with the conservative
regridding matrix (from Task 2.6b) via metadata-driven query methods.

Changes:
- QuantityTypeAspect: Add needs_vertical_normalization() query method
  * Returns true for wet mass mixing ratios (QUANTITY_MIXING_RATIO + BASIS_WET_MASS)
  * Provides metadata-driven decision point for normalization

- VerticalGridAspect: Query QuantityTypeAspect in make_transform()
  * Check if conservative regridding requires normalization
  * Set needs_normalization flag in VerticalRegridParam
  * Gracefully handle absence of QuantityTypeAspect

- VerticalRegridTransform: Enhanced regrid_field_() for fused normalization
  * Accept needs_normalization flag and vertical coordinate fields
  * When normalization needed: normalize by dp, regrid, denormalize
  * Otherwise: standard conservative matrix multiplication
  * Enable vertical coordinate couplers in update() for time-varying coords

This implementation follows Option B (full metadata integration) from
the Task 2.6 specification. The fused normalization ensures mass
conservation for wet mass mixing ratios during vertical regridding.

commit message:
Implement full vertical regridding with alignment support

Task 5: Full vertical regridding with alignment support for different grids

Major changes:
- Refactored VerticalRegridTransform::update() method to reduce nesting
  - Reduced from 3 levels to 1 level (75 → 50 lines)
  - Added type-bound procedures: process_field() and process_fieldbundle()
  - Moved degeneracy check to field level for better organization
- Fixed alignment-based flipping logic
  - DOWN alignment: no flipping (default ESM orientation)
  - UP alignment: flip coordinates and data before/after interpolation
  - Removed incorrect assumptions about coordinate monotonicity
- Added NullTransform optimization in VerticalGridAspect::make_transform()
  - Returns NullTransform when grids AND alignments match
  - Completely eliminates transform overhead for degenerate cases
- Comprehensive test suite with 11 tests covering all alignment/monotonicity combinations:
  1-2: Degenerate case (same grid, flip only) DOWN↔UP
  3-5: Different grids with reversed coordinates and alignments
  6-7: Different grids, same alignment (DOWN→DOWN)
  8-11: All combinations to ensure no assumptions about coordinate monotonicity

All tests passing with NAG compiler (11/11).

Files modified:
- generic3g/transforms/VerticalRegridTransform.F90
- generic3g/specs/VerticalGridAspect.F90
- generic3g/tests/Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf
- .opencode/skills/mapl-build/SKILL.md (updated test workflow)

commit message:
Task 5: Add comprehensive integration tests for normalized regridding (#4546)

* Task 5: Add comprehensive integration tests for normalized regridding

Adds Test_IntegratedNormalization.pf with tests verifying:
- Mass conservation with horizontal conservative regridding
- Non-conservative (bilinear) regridding without normalization overhead
- Full 3D pipeline (horizontal + vertical conservative regridding)

All tests use proper DELP-based mass calculations and verify conservation
within strict tolerances. Tests use PE/DE grid conventions to avoid ESMF
floating point overflow issues with small test grids.

Resolves #4531

* Add normalization mismatch handling test

Adds test_normalization_mismatch() to verify that connection machinery
correctly handles cases where import and export have different
normalizations (NORMALIZE_DELP vs NORMALIZE_NONE).

This baseline test for Task 5 Scenario 5 verifies that connections with
mismatched normalizations complete without error. Full validation of
extension creation and transform generation will be added in Phase 2 when
NormalizationTransform is fully implemented (currently returns NullTransform
as placeholder).

Test creates two registries with specs having different NormalizationAspects,
connects them via SimpleConnection, and verifies the connection succeeds.

* Refactor mass calculation with helper function

- Add calculate_total_mass() helper that uses array slicing and sum()
- Replace verbose triple-nested loops with single function calls
- Improves clarity and maintainability
- All 65 tests still pass

* Add memory efficiency tests for integrated normalization

- Add test_memory_efficiency_matching_grids: verifies no extensions created when grids match
- Add test_memory_efficiency_different_grids: verifies only 1 extension (regrid) with different grids
- Add vertical_grid fixture using BasicVerticalGridSpec to avoid mirror transform issues
- Add create_test_vertical_grid() helper function
- Use VariableSpec with complete aspects (geom + vgrid) to enable proper transform selection
- Tests verify integrated normalization is memory efficient (1 transform vs 3)

All 67 tests passing.

commit message:
Phase 2 Task 2.1: Implement NormalizationAspect with separated metadata (#4448)

This commit implements Phase 2, Task 2.1 of the conservative regridding implementation:
creating NormalizationAspect as an independent aspect with its own metadata type.

Major refactoring from initial design:
- Split normalization properties from QuantityTypeMetadata into separate NormalizationMetadata
- QuantityTypeAspect derives and writes BOTH metadata types to field/bundle info
- NormalizationAspect reads NormalizationMetadata independently
- Ensures aspects are independent with no direct coupling

New files:
- esmf_utils/NormalizationMetadata.F90: Normalization-specific metadata type
- generic3g/specs/NormalizationAspect.F90: Aspect to handle field normalization
- generic3g/tests/Test_NormalizationAspect.pf: Comprehensive test suite (11 tests)

Modified files:
- esmf_utils/QuantityTypeMetadata.F90: Removed normalization fields
- generic3g/specs/QuantityTypeAspect.F90: Added derive_normalization_metadata()
- field/FieldInfo.F90, FieldGet/Set.F90: Added normalization_metadata parameter
- field_bundle/FieldBundleInfo.F90, FieldBundleGet/Set.F90: Added normalization_metadata
- generic3g/specs/AspectId.F90: Added NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID = 10
- generic3g/tests/Test_QuantityTypeAspect.pf: Removed normalization tests (moved to NormalizationAspect)
- generic3g/tests/Test_2DConservativeRegrid.pf: Updated to use NormalizationMetadata

Key architectural decisions:
- NormalizationMetadata constructor requires normalization_type (non-optional) to avoid ambiguity
- Metadata flows: VariableSpec → QuantityTypeAspect → derives both metadata types → writes to field info
- NormalizationAspect and QuantityTypeAspect are completely independent

Builds successfully with NAG compiler. All tests pass.

Add default for missing vector_basis_kind metadata (#4389)

* Add vector basis kind support for regridding

This implements issue #4376 by introducing VectorBasisKind to distinguish
between NS (North-South/geographic) and GRID (grid-relative) vector
components during regridding operations.

Key changes:
- New VectorBasisKind enum (NS, GRID, INVALID) in esmf_utils
- String-based VariableSpec API: vector_basis_kind='NS' or 'GRID'
- Field bundle metadata storage via FieldBundleSet/Get
- Regridder integration: passes basis kind directly to get_basis()
- Validation ensures vector_basis_kind only used with VECTOR bundles
- get_basis() refactored with early returns (no nesting)
- Comprehensive test suite (12 tests covering all scenarios)

User API supports vector_basis_kind='NS' (default for vectors) or 'GRID'.
The enum-based internal API ensures type safety throughout the stack.

* Fix unallocated vector_basis_kind bugs

- VariableSpec: Check allocation before accessing vector_basis_kind
- VariableSpec: Default to VECTOR_BASIS_KIND_NS when unallocated
- FieldBundleCreate: Auto-set NS basis for VECTOR bundles
- Remove unused status variable in verify_deferred_items

* Use itemType to detect vectors in VariableSpec

Addresses reviewer feedback to use the canonical itemType field
instead of heuristics (vector_component_names, standard_name format)
to determine if a VariableSpec represents a vector.

Changes:
- VariableSpec: Check itemType == MAPL_STATEITEM_VECTOR
- Removed complex heuristic logic and unused is_vector variable
- Test_VectorBasisKind: Added itemtype parameter and import

* Add vector_basis_kind for VectorBracket

- Add vector_basis_kind support to VectorBracketClassAspect
- Generalize VectorBracket regridding for any even number of fields
- Simplify vector_basis_kind validation in VariableSpec
- Make vector_basis_kind non-allocatable (always has default value)

* Fix constant name: VECTORBRACKET not VECTOR_BRACKET

Rename MAPL_STATEITEM_VECTOR_BRACKET to MAPL_STATEITEM_VECTORBRACKET
for consistency with naming convention MAPL_STATEITEM_<class> where
the class is VectorBracket (no underscore in compound name).

* Add default for missing vector_basis_kind

When vector_basis_kind metadata is not present in a bundle,
use VECTOR_BASIS_KIND_NS as the default instead of failing.
This makes the code more robust and consistent with how other
optional metadata attributes are handled.

commit message:
Fix HConfig multi-PE mesh decomposition

This commit fixes the test_make_geom_4pe_from_hconfig test by ensuring
that MeshGeomSpec created from HConfig/FileMetadata includes both element
and node distribution for Phase 3 distributed meshes.

Root Cause:
When creating a MeshGeomSpec from HConfig (which reads from FileMetadata),
the decomposition was created using only the element count:
  decomp = make_MeshDecomposition(nelements, _RC)

This creates a decomposition with only point_distribution (elements) but
not node_distribution, which is required for Phase 3 distributed meshes
where nodes are shared across PEs.

Solution:
Updated make_MeshGeomSpec_from_metadata to use the full constructor:
  decomp = MeshDecomposition(nelements, nnodes, petCount=petCount)

This ensures both element and node distributions are set up, enabling
proper Phase 3 mesh creation with node ownership.

Changes:
- geom/Mesh/MeshGeomSpec_smod.F90:
  * Get petCount from current VM
  * Use full MeshDecomposition constructor with both nelements and nnodes
  * This matches the pattern used in working multi-PE tests

- geom/tests/Test_MeshGeomFactory_File.pf:
  * Re-enabled test_make_geom_4pe_from_hconfig

Test Results:
- test_make_geom_4pe_from_hconfig now passes
- Total passing tests: 11 (6 single-PE + 5 multi-PE)
- 5 out of 6 4PE tests now pass
- Only test_make_geom_4pe_uneven_distribution remains disabled

Files Modified:
- geom/Mesh/MeshGeomSpec_smod.F90
- geom/tests/Test_MeshGeomFactory_File.pf

commit message:
Task 3: Enhance GeomAspect for integrated normalization (#4538)

* Enhance GeomAspect to support integrated normalization

Implements Task 3 of the MAPL3 Integrated Normalization Plan (issue #4529).

Key changes:
- Refactored GeomAspect::make_transform using Fortran submodule pattern
  to resolve circular dependency with VerticalGridAspect
- Enhanced make_transform to detect normalization requirements for
  conservative regridding
- Query NormalizationAspect and VerticalGridAspect from aspect map
- Obtain vertical coordinate fields via coupler pattern
- Pass normalization metadata and coordinate info to RegridTransform
- Added get_physical_dimension() method to NormalizationType for
  mapping normalization type to physical dimension name

Implementation notes:
- Uses submodule in generic3g/specs/GeomAspect/make_transform.F90 to
  break circular module dependency
- Extracts helper functions (should_use_normalization,
  build_normalized_regrid_transform) to reduce complexity
- Proper error handling: checks status before using boolean results
- Falls back to standard regridding for non-conservative methods

Resolves #4529

* Export get_regridder_param for submodule access

The make_transform submodule needs to call get_regridder_param, but it
was not accessible because it was private to the module. This caused
linker errors with gfortran (and likely other compilers) during clean
builds, though incremental NAG builds masked the issue.

Fix: Add get_regridder_param to the public exports list.

This fixes the build failure in PR #4538.

* Address PR #4538 review comments

- Use esma_add_fortran_submodules for GeomAspect submodule
- Add 'only' clauses to normalization imports in GeomAspect.F90
- Import NORMALIZE_NONE and operator(==) in submodule

Addresses inline comments from @pchakraborty on PR #4538

commit message:
Fixes #98 - MAPL Code Generator for GridComp specs.

This is the initial implementation of a python package to generate
include files for MAPL GridComps.    Each grid comp has a certain
degree of repetitive declarations related to ESMF import, export, and
interal states.   These are more cleanly expressed and maintained in
a comma-separated-value (CSV) file.   There is a downside though that
developers must now look for this information into a separate file.

This new python layer generates 3 include files for each grid comp
corresponding to

1. calls to MAPL_Add*Spec() for import/export/internal items.
2. calls to MAPL_GetPointer() to relate items to local variables
3. declarations of local variables.

Developers should edit input CSV files with an editor mode that
supports this format.  E.g., csv-mode in emacs or even Excel.
Such tools can show the fields in an aligned fashion withou forcing
the maintainers to adjust spacing with each change.

commit message:
Task 2.4: Add inverse normalization support to NormalizationTransform (#4458)

* Add InverseNormalizationAspect for Task 2.3

Implements InverseNormalizationAspect which reverses normalization
performed by NormalizationAspect. This aspect divides fields by an
auxiliary field (e.g., delp or dz) to convert from extensive per-area
units back to intensive units after regridding.

Key features:
- Mirrors NormalizationAspect API and behavior but performs inverse operation
- Supports division by auxiliary fields (delp, dz) with scale factors
- Includes comprehensive unit tests (14 tests, all passing)
- Registered as INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID (11) in AspectId.F90

This aspect will be used in Phase 2 of conservative regridding to
denormalize fields after vertical regridding is complete.

Fixes #4455

* Refactor: Use single NormalizationAspect class with is_inverse flag

- Eliminate InverseNormalizationAspect.F90 (~458 lines of duplicate code)
- Add is_inverse boolean flag to NormalizationAspect
- Update get_aspect_id() to return correct ID based on is_inverse flag
- Add get_is_inverse() and set_is_inverse() methods
- Add compute_denormalized_units() helper for inverse mode
- Update update_from_payload() to handle both modes
- Update Test_InverseNormalizationAspect.pf to use single class
- Remove InverseNormalizationAspect from CMakeLists.txt

Benefits:
- Eliminates ~458 lines of duplicated code
- Easier to maintain - changes in one place
- Clear separation: aspect ID for type system, boolean for behavior

Issue #4455

* Fix: Store aspect_id as member variable to comply with nopass requirement

- Add aspect_id_value member variable to NormalizationAspect
- Set aspect_id_value in constructor based on is_inverse flag
- Keep get_aspect_id() as nopass (returns default NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID)
- Add get_instance_aspect_id() method to get actual instance's aspect_id
- Update test to use get_instance_aspect_id()

Fixes CI error: 'If either an overriding binding or an overridden binding
has a passed-object dummy argument, then the other must also'

* Refactor: InverseNormalizationAspect extends NormalizationAspect

Architecture:
- NormalizationAspect: base class with all implementation
- InverseNormalizationAspect: thin subclass (~50 lines) that:
  - Extends NormalizationAspect
  - Overrides get_aspect_id() to return INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID
  - Sets is_inverse=.true. in constructor
  - Inherits all other functionality

Benefits:
- Two distinct aspect IDs (enables both in same connection)
- Minimal code duplication (~50 lines vs ~458 in original approach)
- All implementation in one place (maintainability)
- Single Transform class will take boolean for direction (Task 2.4)

Issue #4455

* Fix: Remove invalid 'protected' attribute from type component

The 'protected' attribute is only valid for module-level variables,
not for type components. This was causing a compilation error in CI.

Fixes compilation error: 'This attribute specification is not valid
for a component definition statement. [PROTECTED]'

* Remove private from NormalizationAspect components for subclass access

InverseNormalizationAspect extends NormalizationAspect and needs to
access the is_inverse component. Removing the private statement from
the type definition allows the subclass to access parent components.

This follows the same pattern used in NormalizationTransform.

* Keep components private, pass is_inverse via constructor

Instead of removing private from NormalizationAspect components,
add an optional is_inverse parameter to the constructor. This:

1. Restores private attribute on NormalizationAspect type components
2. Adds optional is_inverse parameter to new_NormalizationAspect()
3. Updates InverseNormalizationAspect to pass is_inverse=.true.
   to parent constructor instead of directly accessing the component

This maintains proper encapsulation while allowing the subclass
to configure the parent's behavior through the constructor.

* Add inverse normalization support to NormalizationTransform (Task 2.4)

Extends NormalizationTransform with optional is_inverse parameter to support
both forward normalization (multiply) and inverse normalization (divide).

Changes:
- Add is_inverse boolean member to NormalizationTransform (default false)
- Update constructor to accept optional is_inverse parameter
- Modify update_field() to divide when is_inverse=true (with zero protection)
- Pass is_inverse through update_field_bundle()
- Support both R4 and R8 typekinds
- Add public export of new_NormalizationTransform function
- Remove private attribute from type components (NAG compiler requirement)

Tests:
- test_denormalize_field_R4: Verify inverse with R4 typekind
- test_denormalize_field_R8: Verify inverse with R8 typekind
- test_division_by_zero_R4: Safe handling of zero denominator
- test_roundtrip_R4: Verify normalize→denormalize recovers original

Division by zero handling: When denominator < epsilon, output = 0.0

Note: Aspects still return NullTransform() - coupler infrastructure
needed to create actual transforms (deferred to future tasks).

Issue: #4457

* Fix test_roundtrip_R4: Add COUPLER_IMPORT_NAME to midState

The midState needs both COUPLER_EXPORT_NAME and COUPLER_IMPORT_NAME
because it serves as:
- Export state for the normalize transform
- Import state for the denormalize transform

Without COUPLER_IMPORT_NAME, the denormalize step fails with
'Mismatched item types' when it can't find the expected field name.

* Fix ESMF_StateAdd syntax: remove array syntax when using itemName

ESMF_StateAdd with itemName parameter doesn't support array syntax.
Use scalar field argument instead of [field_mid] when adding with
custom itemName.

* Fix test_roundtrip_R4: Use separate states for chaining transforms

The rigid COUPLER_IMPORT_NAME/COUPLER_EXPORT_NAME convention prevents
directly chaining transforms through a single intermediate state.

Solution:
- Create separate export and import states for the intermediate value
- Manually copy data between them (simulates what a coupler would do)
- This reveals the architectural constraint that will be resolved
  when coupler support is added (similar to VerticalRegridTransform)

In production, couplers will handle data movement between transforms.
This test demonstrates the need for that infrastructure.

commit message:
Split MAPL.generic3g.tests into 6 logical test suites (#4518)

* Split MAPL.generic3g.tests into 6 logical test suites

Reorganizes the large MAPL.generic3g.tests suite (61 test files, ~11,200 lines) into 6 logical subsets for better organization and parallel execution:

1. MAPL.generic3g.scenarios - Integration test scenarios
2. MAPL.generic3g.transforms - Data transformation tests
3. MAPL.generic3g.vertical - Vertical regridding tests
4. MAPL.generic3g.aspects - Aspect system tests
5. MAPL.generic3g.components - Component specification tests
6. MAPL.generic3g.core - Core functionality tests

All test suites maintain ESSENTIAL label, MAX_PES 4, and required environment variables. Benefits include faster parallel execution and easier identification of failing test categories.

Fixes #4506

* Initialize field values after geometry change in test_propagate_geom

The test checks that changing geometry triggers field reallocation, not
numerical correctness. However, fields created after geom change contain
uninitialized memory from previous tests when running the full suite.

Intel debug mode FPU checking triggers floating invalid exceptions when
TimeInterpolateTransform compares these uninitialized values.

Fix: Initialize field values to 0.0 after MAPL_FieldBundleSet changes
the geometry, ensuring clean memory for subsequent operations.

This fixes the ifx/ifort debug mode test failures in CI.

* Fix CMake dependency order for Ninja build

Move copy_scenarios target definition before it's used as a dependency.
Ninja requires dependencies to be defined before use, while GNU Make
is more lenient. This fixes the ifort/Ninja build failures in CI.

The copy_scenarios target is now defined at the top of the file, right
after add_subdirectory(gridcomps), so it's available when
MAPL.generic3g.scenarios adds it as a dependency.

* Fix parallel build race condition in generic3g tests

Create a shared library MAPL.generic3g.test_common for common test
sources (MockUserGridComp.F90, accumulator_transform_test_common.F90,
MockAspect.F90) to prevent parallel build conflicts when multiple test
suites compile the same files to the same MODULE_DIRECTORY.

This resolves the race condition that caused build failures in
parallel builds, especially with gfortran-15 and Ninja builds, where
module files would conflict:
  'Cannot rename module file mockaspect_mod.smod0 to mockaspect_mod.smod'

The shared library approach ensures these common sources are compiled
once and linked by all test suites, eliminating file conflicts during
parallel builds.

* Fix Ninja build: Remove Fortran_MODULE_DIRECTORY from test executables

The previous commit created a shared library for common test sources but
didn't address the root cause of the Ninja build failure: multiple test
executables trying to write their loader.mod files to the same directory.

Ninja detected this conflict with:
  'ninja: build stopped: multiple rules generate include/MAPL.generic3g/tests/loader.mod'

Each pFUnit test suite generates its own loader.mod file. When all 6 test
suites were configured with the same Fortran_MODULE_DIRECTORY, Ninja saw
6 different rules trying to create the same output file.

Fix: Remove set_target_properties(... Fortran_MODULE_DIRECTORY) from all
6 test executables. Each test suite now uses its own default module
directory, eliminating the conflict. The shared library continues to use
MODULE_DIRECTORY for its common modules.

Unix Makefiles didn't detect this issue, but Ninja enforces strict rules
about multiple targets generating the same output files.

* Add module directory to test_common interface for proper include paths

Test executables linking to the shared library need to find the modules
it generates. By adding target_include_directories with BUILD_INTERFACE,
CMake automatically adds the shared library's module directory to the
include paths of any target that links to it.

Without this, compilation fails with:
  'Fatal Error: Cannot find module MOCKASPECT_MOD'

Verified with NAG + Ninja build locally.

commit message:
Add InverseNormalizationAspect for Task 2.3

Implements InverseNormalizationAspect which reverses normalization
performed by NormalizationAspect. This aspect divides fields by an
auxiliary field (e.g., delp or dz) to convert from extensive per-area
units back to intensive units after regridding.

Key features:
- Mirrors NormalizationAspect API and behavior but performs inverse operation
- Supports division by auxiliary fields (delp, dz) with scale factors
- Includes comprehensive unit tests (14 tests, all passing)
- Registered as INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID (11) in AspectId.F90

This aspect will be used in Phase 2 of conservative regridding to
denormalize fields after vertical regridding is complete.

Fixes #4455

commit message:
Task 2.6: Integrate fused normalization into VerticalRegridTransform (#4479)

This commit completes the integration of Task 2.6 by connecting the
fused normalization capability (from Task 2.6a) with the conservative
regridding matrix (from Task 2.6b) via metadata-driven query methods.

Changes:
- QuantityTypeAspect: Add needs_vertical_normalization() query method
  * Returns true for wet mass mixing ratios (QUANTITY_MIXING_RATIO + BASIS_WET_MASS)
  * Provides metadata-driven decision point for normalization

- VerticalGridAspect: Query QuantityTypeAspect in make_transform()
  * Check if conservative regridding requires normalization
  * Set needs_normalization flag in VerticalRegridParam
  * Gracefully handle absence of QuantityTypeAspect

- VerticalRegridTransform: Enhanced regrid_field_() for fused normalization
  * Accept needs_normalization flag and vertical coordinate fields
  * When normalization needed: normalize by dp, regrid, denormalize
  * Otherwise: standard conservative matrix multiplication
  * Enable vertical coordinate couplers in update() for time-varying coords

This implementation follows Option B (full metadata integration) from
the Task 2.6 specification. The fused normalization ensures mass
conservation for wet mass mixing ratios during vertical regridding.

Related: #4478

commit message:
Task 8: Documentation for Vertical Alignment Feature (#4414)

* Add vertical alignment support for coordinate direction handling

This commit implements Tasks 1 and 2 from the vertical alignment feature:
- Add coordinate_direction to VerticalGrid with VerticalCoordinateDirection type
- Add vertical_alignment to VariableSpec and VerticalGridAspect

New Features:
- VerticalCoordinateDirection enum-like type with constants for upward/downward
- VerticalAlignment enum-like type with constants for with_grid/upward/downward
- Default grid coordinate_direction is 'downward' (GEOS convention)
- Default field vertical_alignment is 'with_grid' (follows grid direction)
- Supports shortcuts 'U'/'D' for upward/downward in string constructors
- VerticalAlignment.resolve() method converts alignment to coordinate direction

Implementation:
- Updated VerticalGrid base class and all implementations (BasicVerticalGrid,
  FixedLevelsVerticalGrid, ModelVerticalGrid)
- Added vertical_alignment field to VariableSpec (user-facing string interface)
- Updated VerticalGridAspect to use typed VerticalAlignment internally
- Added comprehensive unit tests for both coordinate_direction and vertical_alignment

Testing:
- All 44 vertical_grid tests pass on NAG compiler
- All 44 vertical_grid tests pass on GFortran compiler
- New tests verify default values, get/set operations, and string conversions

Related to #4377

* Add implementation plan and updated build skill

* Fix module persistence warning - affects ALL compilers, not just gfortran

* Refactor VerticalRegridTransform constructor to use VerticalRegridParam

Simplify the VerticalRegridTransform constructor by grouping related
configuration parameters into a VerticalRegridParam type, reducing the
parameter count from 10 to 5.

Changes:
- Add VerticalRegridParam type with fields: stagger_in, stagger_out,
  method, src_alignment, dst_alignment, is_degenerate_case
- Refactor new_VerticalRegridTransform() to accept regrid_param instead
  of individual optional parameters
- Update VerticalGridAspect to populate and pass VerticalRegridParam
- Add Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf with degenerate case tests
- Both vertical coordinate fields (v_in_coupler, v_out_coupler) remain
  as direct parameters since they are time-varying runtime data

This follows MAPL's existing RegridParam convention for horizontal
regridding and makes future extensions easier without changing the
constructor signature.

* Support vertical regridding for same grid with different alignments

Implement degenerate case handling in vertical regridding where source
and destination share the same vertical grid but have different field
alignments (e.g., one UP, one DOWN). This is an optimization that uses
simple array operations instead of full regrid matrix computation.

Task 3: Add VerticalAlignment to Field/FieldBundle API
- Move VerticalAlignment from generic3g/specs to vertical_grid module
- Add vert_alignment parameter to Field/FieldBundle create, get, and set
- Store alignment in ESMF_Info metadata with KEY_VERT_ALIGNMENT
- Export alignment types through VerticalGrid_API

Task 4: Implement Degenerate Case in VerticalRegridTransform
- Add VerticalRegridParam type to group regrid configuration
- Refactor constructor to use VerticalRegridParam (reduces params 10→5)
- Add src_alignment, dst_alignment, is_degenerate_case fields
- Implement copy_field_() and copy_field_flipped_() for degenerate case
- Update VerticalGridAspect to detect degenerate case and pass flag
- Add Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf with flip tests

Key design decisions:
- Vertical coordinate fields remain direct parameters (time-varying data)
- Degenerate case detected by grid ID comparison + alignment check
- Same alignment → direct copy, different alignment → vertical flip
- Follows existing RegridParam convention for consistency

Testing:
- 422 generic3g tests pass (16 pre-existing scenario failures)
- New tests verify DOWN→UP and UP→DOWN flips work correctly
- 23 field_bundle tests pass, 20 field tests pass

* Implement full vertical regridding with alignment support

Task 5: Full vertical regridding with alignment support for different grids

Major changes:
- Refactored VerticalRegridTransform::update() method to reduce nesting
  - Reduced from 3 levels to 1 level (75 → 50 lines)
  - Added type-bound procedures: process_field() and process_fieldbundle()
  - Moved degeneracy check to field level for better organization
- Fixed alignment-based flipping logic
  - DOWN alignment: no flipping (default ESM orientation)
  - UP alignment: flip coordinates and data before/after interpolation
  - Removed incorrect assumptions about coordinate monotonicity
- Added NullTransform optimization in VerticalGridAspect::make_transform()
  - Returns NullTransform when grids AND alignments match
  - Completely eliminates transform overhead for degenerate cases
- Comprehensive test suite with 11 tests covering all alignment/monotonicity combinations:
  1-2: Degenerate case (same grid, flip only) DOWN↔UP
  3-5: Different grids with reversed coordinates and alignments
  6-7: Different grids, same alignment (DOWN→DOWN)
  8-11: All combinations to ensure no assumptions about coordinate monotonicity

All tests passing with NAG compiler (11/11).

Files modified:
- generic3g/transforms/VerticalRegridTransform.F90
- generic3g/specs/VerticalGridAspect.F90
- generic3g/tests/Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf
- .opencode/skills/mapl-build/SKILL.md (updated test workflow)

* Add YAML parsing for vertical_alignment in ExtData

- Add vertical_alignment field to ExtDataRule type
- Parse vertical_alignment from YAML configuration
- Update implementation plan to mark Task 6 complete

Enables ExtData YAML files to specify vertical alignment:
  vertical_alignment: upward  # or "downward" or "with_grid"

The field is available in ExtDataRule for future integration
with field configuration and regridding operations.

* Add Task 7 integration test scenarios for vertical alignment

This commit adds three integration test scenarios for vertical alignment support:

1. vertical_alignment_same_grid: Tests degenerate case where same vertical
   grid has fields with different alignments (downward vs upward). Verifies
   copy-with-flip functionality.

2. vertical_alignment_regrid: Tests full vertical regridding with different
   grids (3 levels vs 4 levels) and different field alignments. Verifies
   regridding with appropriate flips.

3. vertical_alignment_with_grid: Tests default 'with_grid' alignment where
   fields automatically use their grid's coordinate_direction. Both grids
   use downward direction.

These scenarios exercise the vertical alignment implementation from Tasks 1-6
and verify proper handling of coordinate_direction and vertical_alignment.

Relates to #4411

* Fix vertical_alignment_regrid test scenario grid range

The destination grid levels [35, 25, 15, 5] were outside the valid
range for vertical regridding. VerticalLinearMap requires that the
destination grid be fully contained within the source grid range.

Changed destination levels to [28, 22, 16, 11] which are properly
contained within the source range [30, 20, 10].

All 24 vertical alignment integration tests now pass.

* Add comprehensive documentation for vertical alignment feature

- Create first formal MAPL3 documentation: docs/mapl3/vertical-alignment.md
  - Conceptual overview of coordinate direction vs. data alignment
  - YAML configuration guide for all alignment options (up, down, auto)
  - Integration with vertical regridding and ExtData
  - Algorithm documentation for alignment resolution
  - Best practices, constraints, and real-world examples

- Add extensive code documentation to VerticalRegridTransform.F90
  - Document alignment canonicalization algorithm
  - Explain degenerate case handling (same grid, different alignments)
  - Add detailed method documentation for initialize, update, process_field
  - Document regrid_field_ data flow and copy_field_flipped_ operation

- Add documentation to VerticalGridAspect.F90
  - Explain degenerate case detection logic
  - Document grid matching algorithm (ID comparison + structural equality)

Closes #4413

* Fix INTENT mismatch in VerticalRegridTransform process_field

Change f_in parameter from intent(in) to intent(inout) in process_field
subroutine. Both copy_field_flipped_ and regrid_field_ require inout
access to get field pointers via assign_fptr_condensed_array.

This fixes NAG compiler errors about argument intent mismatches.

commit message:
Fixes #3264 - Swap ownership of consumer

StateItemExtensions now own the consumers rather than the producers.
This change was motivated by the fact that imports and "final"
extensions need to share the producer, whereas consumers always
associated with a unique item - the one that generates the extension.

Various other interfaces needed to be updated. Primarily many
references to GriddedComponentDriver now need to be refrences to the
abstract parent: ComponentDriver, which is actually a good thing in
and of itself.

commit message:
Task 2.5: Add Primary Coordinate Support to VerticalGrid (#4460)

* Task 2.5: Add primary coordinate support to VerticalGrid

Add metadata to identify primary vertical coordinate for conservative
regridding. This enables the framework to determine which auxiliary
field (DELP or DZ) to use for normalization.

Changes:
- Add primary_coordinate member to VerticalGrid base class
- Add get_primary_coordinate() and set_primary_coordinate() methods
- Returns empty string if not set
- Add 4 comprehensive tests:
  * test_primary_coordinate_default - verify default is empty
  * test_primary_coordinate_set_pressure - set to pressure
  * test_primary_coordinate_set_height - set to height
  * test_primary_coordinate_change - change from one to another

Convention:
- First coordinate added will be primary by default (future enhancement)
- User can override with explicit set_primary_coordinate() call

Implements Task 2.5 from Phase 2 of conservative regridding plan.

* Add Task 2.6b: Conservative Vertical Regridding Matrix Construction

Adds detailed task specification for implementing overlap-based
conservative vertical regridding matrix construction.

Task 2.6b focuses on the core conservative algorithm:
- Overlap-based weight computation using layer interfaces
- Sparse matrix construction (CSR format)
- Conservation validation
- Integration with VerticalRegridTransform

This is distinct from Task 2.6 which handles the fused
normalization/denormalization workflow. Task 2.6 depends on
Task 2.6b being completed first.

Estimated effort: 20 hours

* Remove else clause from get_primary_coordinate

Set default value first, then conditionally override.
Avoids else clause per coding style preference.

author: Tom Clune <thomas.l.clune@nasa.gov>
commit message:
Update implementation plan v2.2: Phase 3 restructuring for ConservationAspect

- Added ConservationAspect architecture (Task 3.0)
  - New ConservationType enum: CONSERVE_MASS, CONSERVE_ENERGY, CONSERVE_MOMENTUM, CONSERVE_NONE
  - Separates 'what is conserved' (physics) from 'how to normalize' (mathematics)
  - Backward compatibility via inference from QuantityTypeAspect

- Refactored NormalizationAspect (Task 3.0)
  - Uses composition pattern with NormalizationMetadata (eliminates duplication)
  - Fixed magic number: replaced tolerance comparison with exact equality (==)
  - Rationale: scale factors are discrete choices, not continuous values

- Phase reordering for better prioritization
  - OLD: Phase 3 = Dry/Wet, Phase 4 = Concentration
  - NEW: Phase 3 = Concentration + ConservationAspect, Phase 4 = Dry/Wet
  - Reason: Concentration support is higher priority and simpler

- Updated effort estimates
  - Phase 3: 46 hours (1-2 weeks)
  - Phase 4: 72 hours (2 weeks)
  - Total: 334 hours for Phases 1-4 (down from 372 hours)

- Document updates
  - Updated all task references throughout
  - Fixed Success Criteria for Phases 3 & 4
  - Updated Appendix B effort summary
  - Updated examples in Appendix A

Related: #4507

commit message:
ci: specify fixed site name for CDash runs in GitHub Actions

GitHub Actions uses random hostnames for each job runner, causing CDash to register each nightly build under a different site. This breaks the contiguous build history timeline. By explicitly passing `-D site="GitHub-Actions"` in the nightly workflow, CDash can properly group and connect the build history. Additionally, added a warning comment in CTestDashboard.cmake reminding developers to explicitly set the site on ephemeral nodes like SLURM, CI, or VPN laptops.

commit message:
Remove pointer-based mesh data and convert to file-based mesh creation

This commit refactors MeshGeomSpec to remove in-memory pointer storage
for mesh data (node_coords, element_conn, num_element_conn, element_mask)
and simplifies mesh creation to use ESMF's file-based path exclusively.

Changes:
- Remove pointer data members and related methods (set_mesh_data, get_node_coords,
  get_connectivity, get_num_element_conn, get_element_mask) from MeshGeomSpec
- Simplify create_esmf_mesh to only create meshes from ESMF-format files using
  ESMF_MeshCreate, supporting both automatic and custom elementDistgrid distribution
- Reduce MeshGeomFactory_smod.F90 create_esmf_mesh from 291 lines to 42 lines
- Update typesafe_make_file_metadata to generate generic metadata without requiring
  connectivity data access
- Add helper functions for hexagon and octagon mesh file creation
- Convert all tests to use file-based mesh creation via MeshTestHelper functions
- Remove backward compatibility tests for programmatic mesh creation
- Move _UNUSED_DUMMY declarations to end of subroutines (before _RETURN)

Test results: All mesh-related tests pass (59/59 single-PE, 15/15 multi-PE)

Net result: -328 lines of code, cleaner architecture, better performance

commit message:
Update MAPL_LatLonGridFactory.F90

Some reprocessed GEOS-Chem input data specifies the first and last latitudes for pole-centered data as instead being at (90 - dlat/2) N/S. This results in MAPL treating the data as being regional, which in turns results in incorrect bilinear interpolation of (eg) wind data at the poles - giving non-physical results. This fix checks specifically for this incorrect latitude specification, correcting it to a conventional "pole-centered" specification if detected.

commit message:
Task 2.7: Update Aspect Ordering for Normalization (#4480)

* Task 2.7: Update aspect ordering for normalization

This commit adds normalization aspects to the coupling order for Field
and FieldBundle classes, ensuring transforms are applied in the correct
sequence for conservative regridding with normalization.

Changes:
- FieldClassAspect: Updated get_aspect_order() to include:
  * QUANTITY_TYPE_ASPECT_ID (after UNGRIDDED_DIMS)
  * NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID (before GEOM_ASPECT for horizontal regrid)
  * INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID (after VERTICAL_GRID for vertical regrid)

- FieldBundleClassAspect: Same aspect ordering updates

New aspect ordering ensures proper transform pipeline:
1. QUANTITY_TYPE_ASPECT_ID - Provides metadata for normalization decisions
2. NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID - Normalize before horizontal regridding
3. GEOM_ASPECT_ID - Horizontal regridding (may be conservative)
4. VERTICAL_GRID_ASPECT_ID - Vertical regridding with fused normalization
5. INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID - Denormalize after vertical regridding
6. UNITS_ASPECT_ID, TYPEKIND_ASPECT_ID - Final conversions

This ordering is required for the complete 3D conservative regridding
workflow introduced in Phase 2 of the conservative regridding plan.

Related: #4478

* Add default normalization aspects to all fields

- Add QuantityTypeAspect, NormalizationAspect, and InverseNormalizationAspect
  to VariableSpec.make_aspects()
- All three aspects are created in mirror/pass-through mode by default
- This ensures all fields have these aspects in their AspectMap, allowing
  the new aspect ordering to function correctly
- Aspects remain in mirror mode unless explicitly configured for
  conservative regridding with normalization

* Fix: Set mirror=false for default normalization aspects

The new aspects (QuantityType, Normalization, InverseNormalization) should
be Category 1 aspects with sensible defaults, not mirror mode:

- QuantityTypeAspect: QUANTITY_UNKNOWN (generic handling, no special processing)
- NormalizationAspect: No normalization parameters (no transform needed)
- InverseNormalizationAspect: No denormalization (no transform needed)

Setting mirror=false ensures both sides of a connection have explicit
default values, avoiding the double-mirror error (case 2 in can_connect_to).
When both have default values, matches() returns true and no transform is created.

If conservative regridding is later requested with QUANTITY_UNKNOWN, we can
error at that point. Eventually FieldDictionary will provide proper defaults.

* Fix NormalizationAspect matches() for default case

When both src and dst have no normalization configured (aux_field_name not
allocated), they should match - both represent "no normalization needed".

Added check: if neither side has aux_field_name allocated, return true.
This handles the Category 1 default case where all fields get a default
NormalizationAspect with no parameters.

* Fix aspect constructors to use Category 1 defaults (mirror=false)

- Changed NormalizationAspect, InverseNormalizationAspect, and QuantityTypeAspect
  constructors to default to mirror=false instead of mirror=true
- These are Category 1 aspects with sensible defaults that don't require mirror mode
- Updated VariableSpec to remove redundant set_mirror calls (now handled in constructors)
- Fixed NormalizationAspect matches() to handle default case (both unallocated)
- Updated test expectations in Test_NormalizationAspect, Test_InverseNormalizationAspect,
  and Test_QuantityTypeAspect to reflect Category 1 behavior
- Tests now explicitly set mirror=true when testing mirror functionality

This fixes connection failures where both sides had mirror=true (double-mirror invalid)

* Revert constructor changes - keep mirror=true as default

- Reverted NormalizationAspect, QuantityTypeAspect, InverseNormalizationAspect constructors back to mirror=true default
- Kept explicit set_mirror(.false.) calls in VariableSpec.make_aspects()
- Reverted test expectations back to expecting mirror=true by default
- This preserves existing behavior while only changing the new aspects created in VariableSpec

* Add diagnostic test for polymorphic set_mirror - PASSES

This test proves that:
1. set_mirror(.false.) works correctly on class(StateItemAspect) variables
2. Two NormalizationAspects with mirror=false can connect

So the 202 test failures must have a different root cause.

* Implement update_payload() for NormalizationAspect to fix mirror flag propagation

- Implemented update_payload() to serialize aspect state into NormalizationMetadata
- Creates mirror metadata when aspect is mirror=true
- Creates non-mirror NORMALIZE_NONE metadata when aspect has no normalization configured
- Creates non-mirror metadata with parameters when aspect has normalization (DELP/DZ)
- Simplified update_from_payload() to follow UngriddedDimsAspect pattern
- Added roundtrip tests: update_payload -> update_from_payload for mirror and non-mirror cases
- Fixes issue where aspects created with mirror=false in VariableSpec were being overwritten to mirror=true

This fix ensures that default NormalizationAspects created in VariableSpec maintain their
Category 1 (non-mirror) status through the payload serialization/deserialization cycle.

* Fix NormalizationAspect update_payload() to not overwrite QuantityTypeAspect metadata

- Changed update_payload() to only write normalization_metadata when aspect is mirror
  OR has explicit normalization configuration (aux_field_name allocated)
- When non-mirror with no explicit configuration (Category 1 default), leave metadata
  as-is to preserve what QuantityTypeAspect may have written
- This prevents NormalizationAspect from overwriting normalization metadata derived
  from QuantityType with generic NORMALIZE_NONE
- Aspect order: QuantityTypeAspect writes first, NormalizationAspect optionally overrides

* Fix NormalizationAspect serialization to preserve QuantityTypeAspect metadata

This commit fixes two issues related to the new aspect ordering:

1. NormalizationAspect.update_payload() now correctly handles the interaction
   with QuantityTypeAspect by reading existing metadata before deciding whether
   to write. This preserves the normalization metadata derived from quantity
   types when NormalizationAspect has no explicit configuration.

2. VariableSpec.add_item() now supports the three new aspect types
   (QuantityTypeAspect, NormalizationAspect, InverseNormalizationAspect)
   in its select type statement.

Test Results:
- Test_Couplers_suite: 2/2 passing (was 0/2)
- Test_Scenarios_suite: 202/218 passing (was 26/218)
- Remaining 16 failures are in vertical_regridding scenarios and appear
  to be caused by some StateItemSpecs missing the new aspects entirely.
  This requires further investigation.

The update_payload() fix ensures that:
- Mirror aspects always write mirror metadata
- Non-mirror aspects with explicit config write their config
- Non-mirror aspects without explicit config preserve existing metadata
  (which may have been written by QuantityTypeAspect)
- Only overwrites when necessary (mirror mode, explicit config, or existing is mirror)

Related to: Task 2.7 - Update Aspect Ordering for Normalization
Issue: #4478
PR: #4480

* Add new aspects to ModelVerticalGrid coordinate fields

ModelVerticalGrid.get_coordinate_field() manually creates StateItemSpecs
for vertical coordinate fields (PLE, ZLE) but was only adding the old
aspects. This caused vertical_regridding test failures because coordinate
fields were missing QuantityTypeAspect, NormalizationAspect, and
InverseNormalizationAspect.

Add all three new aspects with mirror=false for Category 1 behavior.

Fixes remaining 16 test failures in Test_Scenarios_suite.
All 220 tests now pass (218 scenarios + 2 couplers).

* Fix units allocation in NormalizationAspect.update_from_payload()

Check if units variable is allocated before assignment. When a field/bundle
is created without units set, MAPL_FieldGet/MAPL_FieldBundleGet returns
an unallocated units string. Assigning unallocated to source_units caused
runtime error in tests.

Now defaults to empty string if units not allocated.

Fixes runtime error in test_update_payload_then_from_payload_with_normalization.
All 539 tests now pass.

commit message:
Baby steps towards oomph.
  - Partial refactoring of old VarConnPoint.
  - Introduced gFTL VarConnVector
  - Split types into separate files.
    It can be hard to find the definitions of types when they are not
    tied to an obvious module/file.  This is particularly true in
    light of some recent refactorings that left chaos in their wake.
    Current MAPL style guidelines points to a natural solution.
  - Introduced fine-grained specs.

    . Legacy VarSpecType has a long laundry list of components.  Some
      rarely used; some never used. And worse, some that no one even
      recalls what they are for.

    . New specs are more targeted and hierarchical.  E.g., DimsSpec
      has spec components for horizontal, vertical, and ungridded
      dimensions.

    . Mostl likely these new specs will be just "structs" with no
      methods.  But at least one component (possibly otherwise unused)
      should remain private to prevent use of default constructors.

    . Legacy VarSpecType now has a FieldSpec component that is
      initialized during the VarSpecType component.

  - Consolidated new files in ./oomph
  - Also changed namespace to "oomph" from "mapl.

commit message:
Fix field dict init: use inquire() to avoid thrown exception

Catching a non-zero rc after calling load_field_dictionary() does
not suppress the pFUnit exception already thrown by MAPL_Verify
inside the call. Use Fortran inquire() to check file existence
before attempting to open, so ESMF_HConfigCreate is never called
on a missing file and no exception is thrown.

Behavior:
- Default path absent: warn + continue (no exception)
- Explicit path absent: hard fail via _ASSERT
- File present: load normally via _RC

author: Tom Clune <thomas.l.clune@nasa.gov>
commit message:
Initialize fields with sentinel values

Replace zero initialization with sentinel values to catch
uninitialized field usage and ensure deterministic behavior.

Implementation:
- Real fields (R4/R8): IEEE signaling NaN
- Integer fields (I4/I8): -HUGE() sentinel value
- Added initialize_field_sentinel() in FieldCreate and FieldDelta
- Initialize counter fields to 0 in MeanTransform

This change makes debugging easier by ensuring uninitialized
data has a predictable value rather than arbitrary memory contents.

Fixes #4522

ESMF type, but defines its own parameters with the `MAPL` namespace

theirs.   E.g., `MAPL_STATEITEM_FIELD = ESMF_STATEITEM_FIELD`.

commit message:
Refactor VerticalRegridTransform constructor to use VerticalRegridParam

Simplify the VerticalRegridTransform constructor by grouping related
configuration parameters into a VerticalRegridParam type, reducing the
parameter count from 10 to 5.

Changes:
- Add VerticalRegridParam type with fields: stagger_in, stagger_out,
  method, src_alignment, dst_alignment, is_degenerate_case
- Refactor new_VerticalRegridTransform() to accept regrid_param instead
  of individual optional parameters
- Update VerticalGridAspect to populate and pass VerticalRegridParam
- Add Test_VerticalRegridTransform.pf with degenerate case tests
- Both vertical coordinate fields (v_in_coupler, v_out_coupler) remain
  as direct parameters since they are time-varying runtime data

This follows MAPL's existing RegridParam convention for horizontal
regridding and makes future extensions easier without changing the
constructor signature.

commit message:
Refactor: InverseNormalizationAspect extends NormalizationAspect

Architecture:
- NormalizationAspect: base class with all implementation
- InverseNormalizationAspect: thin subclass (~50 lines) that:
  - Extends NormalizationAspect
  - Overrides get_aspect_id() to return INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID
  - Sets is_inverse=.true. in constructor
  - Inherits all other functionality

Benefits:
- Two distinct aspect IDs (enables both in same connection)
- Minimal code duplication (~50 lines vs ~458 in original approach)
- All implementation in one place (maintainability)

commit message:
Task 2.3: Add InverseNormalizationAspect (#4456)

* Add InverseNormalizationAspect for Task 2.3

Implements InverseNormalizationAspect which reverses normalization
performed by NormalizationAspect. This aspect divides fields by an
auxiliary field (e.g., delp or dz) to convert from extensive per-area
units back to intensive units after regridding.

Key features:
- Mirrors NormalizationAspect API and behavior but performs inverse operation
- Supports division by auxiliary fields (delp, dz) with scale factors
- Includes comprehensive unit tests (14 tests, all passing)
- Registered as INVERSE_NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID (11) in AspectId.F90

This aspect will be used in Phase 2 of conservative regridding to
denormalize fields after vertical regridding is complete.

Fixes #4455

* Refactor: Use single NormalizationAspect class with is_inverse flag

- Eliminate InverseNormalizationAspect.F90 (~458 lines of duplicate code)
- Add is_inverse boolean flag to NormalizationAspect
- Update get_aspect_id() to return correct ID based on is_inverse flag
- Add get_is_inverse() and set_is_inverse() methods
- Add compute_denormalized_units() helper for inverse mode
- Update update_from_payload() to handle both modes
- Update Test_InverseNormalizationAspect.pf to use single class
- Remove InverseNormalizationAspect from CMakeLists.txt

Benefits:
- Eliminates ~458 lines of duplicated code
- Easier to maintain - changes in one place
- Clear separation: aspect ID for type system, boolean for behavior

Issue #4455

* Fix: Store aspect_id as member variable to comply with nopass requirement

- Add aspect_id_value member variable to NormalizationAspect
- Set aspect_id_value in constructor based on is_inverse flag
- Keep get_aspect_id() as nopass (returns default NORMALIZATION_ASPECT_ID)
- Add get_instance_aspect_id() method to get actual instance's aspect_id
